result:
Both integrate changes from one branch into another. Difference is history shape.

**`git merge`**: joins two branches with a new merge commit (two parents). Existing commits unchanged. History shows the true branching. Non-destructive.

**`git rebase`**: replays your commits on top of the target branch as new commits with new SHAs. History becomes linear, no merge commit. Rewrites history.

Practical effects:
- Conflicts: merge resolves once. Rebase may ask per replayed commit.
- Log: merge keeps branch context but gets noisy. Rebase reads clean but hides when work really branched.
- Safety: never rebase commits others have already pulled. Their history diverges from yours and you must force-push.

Rule of thumb: rebase local unpushed work onto `main` to tidy it. Merge for shared branches and for landing a feature branch.
